overview.description: Buy Your Card (also known as Substitution) is a stud poker variant where players can pay to exchange cards for better ones. Players are dealt 5 cards (2 down, 3 up) and can buy replacement cards from four options at different prices. High-low game with declaration.

history.origins: Buy Your Card is a poker variant that emerged as part of the family of stud poker games with buying mechanics. These games became popular in home games and private poker clubs as alternatives to standard stud and draw poker.
timeline: Early-mid 20th century: Stud poker variants with buying mechanics developed
Late 20th century: Gained popularity in home games
Modern era: Played in private games and some online platforms
history.evolution: The game evolved from five-card stud, adding the buying mechanic to give players more control over their hands. The Substitution variant simplifies this by removing the price element and allowing free exchanges.
history.cultural: Buy Your Card and similar buying poker variants are popular in home games where players enjoy the additional strategic layer of deciding whether to invest more chips to improve their hands.

setup.players: 2-6 players (Buy Your Card); up to 10 (Substitution variant)
setup.equipment: 52-card deck, poker chips for betting and buying
setup.dealing: Each player gets 5 cards: 2 face down (hole cards) and 3 face up. Dealer places 3 cards face up in a row and the deck face down at the end. Card prices: furthest=1 unit, middle=2 units, nearest deck=3 units, top of deck (unknown)=4 units.

rules.objective: Form the best 5-card high hand, low hand, or both (declaration). Win the pot by having the best hand at showdown or by making others fold.
rules.gameplay: Three rounds of buying, each followed by betting. Buying round: players in turn choose to (1) Buy a card - discard one and buy a replacement (pay price to pot), (2) Stand pat, or (3) Fold. Face-up cards bought are replaced immediately (except last player's purchase). Face-down deck cards stay face down. Betting rounds begin with player showing best hand. After third betting round, surviving players declare high/low/both then showdown.
keyRules: 3 buying rounds, each followed by betting
Must maintain at least 2 hole cards
Face-up cards replaced when bought; deck cards stay face down
High-low with declaration after final betting
Best hand showing starts betting rounds

strategy.basic: Only buy cards when the improvement significantly helps your hand. Consider the cost vs potential return. With a weak hand showing, buying may be expensive as others may raise. In high-low, decide early which direction to pursue or whether to go for both.
strategy.intermediate: Track visible cards to calculate odds of improving. Consider what opponents are buying - if they're buying high cards they likely want high; if buying low cards they want low. The 4-unit unknown card is risky but hides your intentions. Balance the cost of buying against the pot size.
strategy.advanced: Use buying to mislead opponents - buying a face-up card reveals information. Sometimes buying a card you don't need can confuse opponents about your hand direction. Calculate expected value of each purchase based on pot odds and probability of winning. In declaration, read opponents' betting patterns to determine if they're going high, low, or both.
tips: Don't over-invest in buying - chips spent buying don't count as bets
The 4-unit face-down card keeps your intentions hidden
Watch what cards opponents buy for tells about their hand direction
Going for both high and low is risky but very profitable if successful
Consider folding early if buying would be too expensive
Replace your weakest cards first when buying
In Substitution variant (no cost), exchange more liberally

phases.label: Ante
phases.notes: All players post the ante. One unit equals the ante and minimum bet.

phases.label: Deal and Market Setup
phases.notes: Dealer deals 5 cards to each player (2 down, 3 up), then places 3 face-up cards in a row and the deck face down at the end.

phases.label: Buy Round 1
phases.notes: Each player may buy one of the four cards on offer (3 face-up or top of deck), stand pat, or fold. Face-up cards replaced immediately except last player's purchase.

phases.label: Betting Round 1
phases.notes: Player with best hand showing starts the betting.

phases.label: Buy Round 2
phases.notes: Second round of buying. Players must keep at least two hole cards.

phases.label: Declaration
phases.notes: Surviving players declare high, low, or both simultaneously before showdown.

phases.label: Showdown
phases.notes: All active players reveal hands. Pot split per declarations. Pig Rule applies to Both.

ante.description: Post the mandatory ante before cards are dealt. One unit equals the ante and minimum bet.
ante.constraints: Required for each player at start of hand.

deal.description: Dealer deals 5 cards to each player: 2 face down (hole cards) and 3 face up.
deal.constraints: Dealer only. Performed at start of hand after ante.

reveal_market.description: Dealer places 3 cards face up in a row and the undealt deck face down at the end of the row. The four buying options are: furthest card 1 unit, middle 2 units, next to deck 3 units, top of deck 4 units.

buy_market.description: Discard one card from hand and buy one of the three face-up cards to replace it. Pay 1, 2, or 3 units to the pot depending on position (furthest to nearest). Replacement stays face up if replacing an upcard, face down if replacing a hole card. Must keep at least two hole cards.
buy_market.constraints: During a buy round. Choose one of the three face-up cards. Price by position: 1, 2, or 3 units.

buy_stock.description: Discard one card from hand and buy the unknown top card of the deck for 4 units. You look at it but keep it face down. Must keep at least two hole cards.
buy_stock.constraints: During a buy round. Takes the top card of the deck blind.

fold.description: Throw away your cards face down and take no further part in the hand. Forfeit all claim to the pot.
fold.constraints: Available during any buy round or betting round.

check.description: Pass action to next player without betting.
check.constraints: Only legal when no bet has been opened in the current betting round.

call.description: Match the current highest open bet to stay in the hand.
call.constraints: Only legal when a bet or raise exists in the current round.

bet.description: Open betting by placing the minimum bet.
bet.constraints: Only legal when no bet opened yet in the current round. Player with best hand showing starts the betting.

raise.description: Increase the current bet above the existing open bet.
raise.constraints: Only legal when a bet or raise exists. Subject to agreed betting limits.

declare.description: Secretly declare high, low, or both (e.g. chips in fist: 0=Low, 1=High, 2=Both). All surviving players reveal declarations simultaneously. Pig Rule: declaring Both and failing to win both halves forfeits entire pot share.
declare.constraints: All active players declare simultaneously after the final betting round.

reveal_hand.description: Reveal all hole cards face up for showdown.
reveal_hand.constraints: At showdown for all active players.

award_pot.description: Dealer evaluates hands per declarations and splits pot between high and low winners. Pig Rule applied to Both declarers who fail.
award_pot.constraints: Dealer only. After all hands revealed.

play_card.reason: Buy Your Card is stud poker with buying; players do not play cards to a trick or table.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

discard.reason: This game has no discard pile.

pass.reason: This game has no pass action.

bid.reason: This game has no bid action.

edgeCases.text: A player declaring Both who does not win both high and low receives no share of either half.
If the last player in a buying round buys a face-up card, it is not replaced until after the ensuing betting round.
Players must always have at least two cards face down (hole cards).

customActions.description: Do not buy a card; keep your hand as it is for this buy round.
customActions.constraints: Available during any buy round when it is your turn.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for this poker variant where players may buy a card substitution (e.g. replace one card from the deck) before showdown.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Suits do not affect hand rank; standard poker hand rankings apply. After the draw or deal, a player may pay to substitute one card from the deck for one in hand.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit in standard poker order: ace high, then king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two. Standard hand rankings (high card to royal flush) apply; the buy-your-card option may improve the hand before showdown.
engine.dealPattern: 2 down (hole cards), 3 up. Then dealer places 3 face-up market cards and deck at end.

scoring.description: Standard poker hand rankings for high. Low is ace-to-five (wheel is best low). Players declaring both must win both halves or win nothing (scoop attempt). Split pot for high/low if different winners.
scoring.winCondition: Form the best 5-card high hand, low hand, or both (declaration). Win the pot by having the best hand at showdown or by making others fold.
scoring.splitRules: Pot split between best high hand and best low hand (ace-to-five). If a player declares Both and wins both halves they scoop; if they declare Both and fail either half they receive nothing (Pig Rule). Odd chip to high.
